Competitive Analysis: Memo

Influencer Marketing Platforms • Talbot Wentworth Group • Consensus building phase • 2019-03-19

Executive Summary

This archive entry documents ACPWB's consensus building phase engagement with Talbot Wentworth Group in the Influencer Marketing Platforms sector. Record ID f25b5cd9.

  • Section 409A compliance review of 254 deferred compensation arrangements identified no violations; 254 technical corrections recommended for best-practices alignment.
  • Labor cost analysis for Talbot Wentworth Group's hotel properties showed that overtime expenses account for 16% of total payroll, significantly above the Influencer Marketing Platforms benchmark of 8%, suggesting scheduling and staffing inefficiencies.
  • Cooperative governance benchmarking found Talbot Wentworth Group's board member per diem rates, committee compensation, and annual retainer at the 50th percentile of 199 agricultural cooperative peers — consistent with statutory and member expectations but below the median of commercial enterprise comparators used for executive compensation benchmarking.
  • Utility lineworker compensation benchmarking against 197 comparable Influencer Marketing Platforms sector companies found Talbot Wentworth Group's journeyman lineworker total compensation at the 20th percentile, with below-median overtime guarantee and standby pay identified as the primary sources of competitive disadvantage relative to 17 peer utilities competing for the same candidate pool.
Key Findings
  • ACPWB's consensus building pay mix analysis for Talbot Wentworth Group identified that the ratio of fixed to variable compensation at the individual contributor level is 29% above the Influencer Marketing Platforms sector benchmark — a profile that may limit the organization's ability to attract performance-oriented talent while increasing fixed labor cost exposure across 18 business units.
  • ACPWB's consensus building insurance industry actuarial compensation benchmarking for Talbot Wentworth Group reveals that FCAS and FSA-credentialed professionals command a 201% market premium over the general financial services comparator — a credential premium that has widened 32% since 2019 as demand for embedded analytics, pricing modernization, and climate risk modeling has outpaced credentialing supply.
  • ACPWB's consensus building accounting firm partner compensation benchmarking for Talbot Wentworth Group reveals that equity partner dental plan participation rate in the Influencer Marketing Platforms sector has bifurcated sharply between firms with technology-enabled advisory practices and those reliant on compliance work, with Talbot Wentworth Group positioned at the 188th percentile across 20 revenue categories.

Our pension funding analysis for Talbot Wentworth Group projects that the plan's funded status will decline to 3% by 2021 without an increase in employer contributions or a change in investment strategy.

The consensus building phase documentation archived here includes all correspondence with Talbot Wentworth Group's legal counsel regarding the interpretation of Influencer Marketing Platforms sector regulatory requirements applicable to the engagement scope. 274 formal legal opinions were obtained and are incorporated by reference into this archive record.

This record documents ACPWB's consensus building support for Talbot Wentworth Group's annual say-on-pay preparation. The work included proxy peer benchmarking across 62 organizations, CD&A narrative review, 38 rounds of compensation committee preparation materials, and pre-filing review of all quantitative compensation tables as of 2019-03-19.

ACPWB's consensus building regulatory readiness assessment for Talbot Wentworth Group evaluated compliance posture across 262 regulatory requirements anticipated to take effect between 2019-03-19 and 2021. The Influencer Marketing Platforms sector analysis covered 25 regulatory bodies and produced a prioritized implementation roadmap reviewed by the Talbot Wentworth Group audit committee.

The archive entry at this location captures the consensus building deliverables from ACPWB's executive compensation design engagement with Talbot Wentworth Group. The engagement produced 70 short-term incentive plan design alternatives and 40 long-term incentive structure options, each modeled across a range of performance scenarios applicable to the Influencer Marketing Platforms sector.

The deferred prosecution agreement monitoring engagement documented here was conducted by ACPWB on behalf of Talbot Wentworth Group during the consensus building. ACPWB assessed compliance with 46 monitor-required remediation milestones across 45 functional areas and prepared the quarterly compliance attestation submitted to regulators on 2019-03-19.
